description:
#157 compared this list's EF 3.1 factors against a second implementation -- GreenDelta's, shipped for openLCA inside BAFU's 2026 v1 distribution -- by hand, in a script nobody can re-run. Six substances came back where GreenDelta's number is a real EF 3.1 number belonging to a different chemical or a different compartment. This ingests that implementation, so the comparison is a table in the build rather than a script somebody wrote once.

It is a fourth `implemented_by` and it decides nothing. `data/lcia-impact-categories.json` says `decides: true` of the two the consensus implementation is derived from -- the JRC's and ecoinvent's -- and `decides: false` of GreenDelta's: no number of theirs is evidence for one of ours, and none reaches a curator's queue. The measure below says so, by bounding the consensus factor count at what it is without the implementation.

Their package identifies flows by the ecoinvent UUID it was built against, declaring compatibility with ecoinvent 3.6 to 3.11, so a flow of theirs is resolved through the manifest's `resolve_through` chain: 1,144 through ecoinvent 3.12, 50 through 3.8, 29 are EF 3.1 flows already, and 558 name a substance under a spelling of their own and reach nothing.

Measured on the build of 2026-08-25 (`20260825T1354430622920000`, commit `1c1385b`) characterised at `13:00` on 2026-08-28. Every claim below fails on `main`, where the implementation does not exist.

The consensus count was re-measured for #349 on the full build of 2026-08-29 (`20260829T1158418340740000`, commit `505ba28`, all four source lists): 323,890 rather than 324,694, because #163 took 801 of the JRC's factors off retired identifiers between the two builds. The same 323,890 comes out of that morning's three-list build and of the four-list build before #166 and #346 landed, so the count depends neither on Stepwise being merged nor on the second method being published. It is stated as an upper bound now, for the reason the claim itself gives.

expectations.title: GreenDelta's implementation of EF 3.1 is published beside the other three
expectations.comment:
22,342 of the 26,179 factors their package states, over 1,188 consensus flows. The gap is the 558 flows that reach nothing, which carry 3,378 factors; each is a `flow-not-reached` finding naming the substance GreenDelta wrote, so the shortfall is readable rather than silent.

`at_least` rather than an equality: closing part of that gap -- by resolving their names against BAFU's own flows, which is the obvious next step -- should not fail this claim.

expectations.title: Four implementations of 25 categories are published, not three
expectations.comment: `implemented_by` is a field on the category, so a fourth implementation is 25 more category rows rather than a column somewhere. 75 before this change.

expectations.title: Adding a third publisher's numbers changes no factor this list publishes
expectations.comment:
The claim that GreenDelta's implementation is comparison and not evidence, stated as the count it must not exceed: 323,890 on the build of 2026-08-29 (`20260829T1158418340740000`), the same count `main` publishes without them. It is the only measure in this file that would fail if `derive` were handed the wider mapping, which is why it is stated as a bound rather than left to a code review.

An upper bound and not an equality, which is #349. A number going *up* is the failure this file is about -- a factor of theirs becoming one of ours -- and the bound catches it. A number going *down* is one of the two deciding implementations losing factors of its own, which is not about GreenDelta at all: this file, #165's and #347's each wrote the same integer on both sides, so #163 taking 801 of the JRC's factors off retired identifiers failed all three at once, and read as *a GreenDelta number became one of ours*. What the movement was is recorded in `expectations/baseline.json`, which is where a total that moves belongs. Moved to 323,898 with the AGRIBALYSE stack (#188): giving Beta-cyfluthrin the product's own registry number took ecoinvent's rows off the consensus `Cyfluthrin` flows, and the ecoinvent Centre's factors followed its flows -- 64 arrive on the Beta-cyfluthrin substance, 40 leave with the vacated ecoinvent-compartment Cyfluthrin copies, pair-identical amounts, measured on the stack build of d98a075 (1 September 2026). That is +24 against the 323,874 the #178/#826 retirements left, none of it a comparison implementation reaching the consensus -- the movement is one deciding implementation's numbers following its own renamed substance, which is the accounting this guard exists to force. (This file's 323,890 had also gone quietly stale: an upper bound tolerates a fall, so the #178/#826 retirements that made the count 323,874 never forced an edit here.) Moved again on 2026-09-01 when the context convention in `data/context-carry-rules.json` began carrying 1,482 more factors into the contexts nobody characterised -- a river taking surface water's number, silvicultural soil taking non-agricultural soil's -- on top of the 323,898 the cyfluthrin split left: 325,380, the two movements measured on different builds and added, until the next full build records the count. A carried number is this list's own convention applied to a number it already published, not a third publisher's number becoming ours, which is still what this bound is about.

Recorded at 327,064 on the first five-list full build (2 September 2026, `944b274`, merge run `b348667251b34a60af31b157950e9d32`), which is the full build the previous sentence was waiting for. The convention's carry came to 1,866 factors over the four-list baseline's 1,491 (3,357 `carried`), not the 1,482 measured on a branch, because AGRIBALYSE's merge added flows in contexts the convention carries into; `sole` moved by 24 the other way. `adopted` stayed at 1,334, which is the number this bound is really watching: nothing a third publisher stated became ours.

expectations.title: MCPA in agricultural soil: the report holds our 418.35 against GreenDelta's 104.38
expectations.comment:
The worked example of what the comparison is for. 104.38 is EF 3.1's own number for **MCPA-sodium**, the sodium salt, which this list publishes under that name; this flow is the free acid, and the JRC and ecoinvent both state 418.35 for it. Neither file says which the row is about, and this claim is what makes the disagreement a row in `lcia_differences` rather than a thing somebody noticed once.

The number is GreenDelta's and is republished unchanged. This project asserts nothing here about which is right -- #157 argues ours is the better-attested reading, and that argument is not what this file holds.

expectations.title: `Oils, Unspecified` in forest soil: two readings of a compartment EF does not have
expectations.comment: The one of #157's six where the other reading is arguable rather than mistaken. EF 3.1 has no forest soil; GreenDelta reads it as *unspecified* soil and this list reads it as non-agricultural soil, which is what 575 of the 576 substances carrying a forest-soil factor for this category do. Two defensible readings of a missing compartment, and the point of the report is that a reader can see both.

expectations.title: A flow ecoinvent 3.12 no longer ships is still reached, through 3.8
expectations.comment:
GreenDelta's package is built against ecoinvent 3.6 to 3.11 and this list's ecoinvent implementation is read from 3.12, so a chain rather than one release: 3.12 first, then 3.8, then EF 3.1. The 50 flows only 3.8 reaches are the aircraft cruise-height emissions and the ore-grade copper and gold that 3.12 dropped -- all of them the same substance under both releases.

The order is the guard against the other failure: one flow, Flupyrsulfuron-methyl, resolves to *different* consensus flows in the two releases, and 3.12 winning is what decides it. A chain that tried 3.8 first would move four factors onto another flow with nothing saying so.
